question: Can a bounded longer ConvNeXt-Tiny CBAM training package improve its fixed five-model ensemble contribution?
initialization: fresh cached ImageNet weights; new CBAM and seven-class linear classifier
attention_location: final 768-channel spatial feature map before global pooling
head: GAP; native ConvNeXt LayerNorm; flatten; dropout; linear7
preprocessing: PIL RGB; square224 bilinear antialias; ImageNet normalization
augmentation: training only: horizontal flip p0.5, vertical flip p0.5, uniform quarter-turn0/90/180/270
inference: FP32 identity view; no TTA; no multiresolution
imbalance: training-only sqrt inverse-frequency weights normalized to mean1
loss_reduction: weighted numerator divided by target-weight sum across the whole effective batch
sampling: natural training cohort shuffled; no oversampling
warmup_rule: attention and final linear train; frozen features/native LayerNorm, backbone eval; same optimizer carried into full fine-tuning
fusion_rule: replace only S53 Tiny with S79 accuracy-selected checkpoint; other four checkpoints fixed; equal0.2 weights
fusion_search: one post-training selected-checkpoint comparison; no ensemble epoch/weight search
scope: one candidate training package and one fixed ensemble; not a pure CBAM ablation
